name: exa
label: Exa
note: Exa's search and contents API, the whole of it behind one bearer key.

name: firecrawl
label: Firecrawl
note: Firecrawl's scrape and crawl API. Pages it fetches are governed the same as any other reply, so what a crawl brings back is inspected before your application sees it.

name: tavily
label: Tavily
note: Tavily's search and extract API, which is where an agent's web results come from.

name: youcom
label: You.com
note: You.com's Search, Answer and Research API. Every endpoint is a POST, so both the query going out and the pages coming back cross this address. The older ydc-index.io host is a second address and is not this entry.

name: jina-reader
label: Jina Reader
note: Jina's Reader, which turns a URL into text a model can read; the page being fetched is the path, so the request itself names it. Reader answers without a key at a lower rate limit, so an unauthenticated call here is not an error.

name: jina-search
label: Jina Search
note: Jina's search endpoint, which returns whole pages rather than links. Same key as Reader but a separate host, so it is stored as its own upstream.

name: linkup
label: Linkup
note: Linkup's search API. Linkup also accepts payment per request over x402 with no account at all; that path carries no API key and nothing here recognises it.

name: parallel
label: Parallel
note: Parallel's Task and Search APIs for web research. A task runs asynchronously, so what an agent sends and what it collects later are two separate calls and two separate receipts.

name: searchapi
label: SearchApi
note: SearchApi's SERP endpoints for Google and other engines. Its api_key query parameter is the other documented placement; we send the bearer header so the key stays out of the URL and out of logs.

name: search1api
label: Search1API
note: Search1API's search, news and crawl endpoints behind one bearer key.

name: perplexity
label: Perplexity Sonar
note: Perplexity's Sonar API, which answers from a live web search rather than from a fixed corpus. Receipts record it as an ordinary HTTP call, so a Sonar answer is governed as a reply body and not as a model's token stream.

name: perigon
label: Perigon
note: Perigon's news and company search API. It also reads an apiKey query parameter, which we never set: a key in a URL is a key in every proxy log between here and there.

name: apitube
label: APITube
note: APITube's news search. A test key answers with the real response shape and spends no quota, and both key shapes are recognised here, so a receipt from a test key is still a receipt of a real request.

name: newsapi
label: NewsAPI
note: NewsAPI's headline and article search. Its developer plan refuses requests from a server rather than a browser, so a key on that plan will be rejected at the provider whatever we send.

name: semanticscholar
label: Semantic Scholar
note: Semantic Scholar's Graph API for academic search. The API answers without a key from a shared pool, so storing one here buys a rate limit rather than access.

name: ahrefs
label: Ahrefs
note: Ahrefs' v3 API for search-ranking and backlink data. It is read-only data about other people's sites, so what matters in a receipt here is the query, not the reply.

name: apify
label: Apify
note: Apify's REST API: running an actor, and reading the dataset it produced. Apify also accepts the token as a ?token= parameter and its own documentation calls that the less secure of the two; we send the header. The Apify MCP server is a separate entry.

name: brightdata
label: Bright Data
note: Bright Data's API for its SERP, Unlocker and dataset products. Bright Data's acceptable-use policy forbids reselling its proxies without written approval, so this covers a customer's own key carrying their own traffic and nothing else.

name: spider
label: Spider
note: Spider's crawl, scrape and search API. Spider answers unauthenticated requests at 25 a day, so a missing key here fails as a rate limit rather than as a refusal.

name: scrapingbee
label: ScrapingBee
note: ScrapingBee's HTML API, which renders a page and returns it. The api_key query parameter still works and is the older shape; we send the bearer header ScrapingBee now documents, so the key never appears in a URL.

name: scrapingant
label: ScrapingAnt
note: ScrapingAnt's browser-rendered scrape endpoint. The same name works as a query parameter and as a header; the header is what we set.

name: hasdata
label: HasData
note: HasData's SERP and web-scraping endpoints. Each call fetches a page live, so the reply is somebody else's content arriving in your application and is governed as such.

name: browseai
label: Browse AI
note: Browse AI's v2 API, which runs a recorded robot against a site and returns what it captured.

name: browserbase
label: Browserbase
note: Browserbase's REST API for creating and reading cloud browser sessions. What the browser itself does travels over a separate CDP WebSocket that never crosses this address, so a receipt here covers the session's control plane and not the pages it visited.

name: hyperbrowser
label: Hyperbrowser
note: Hyperbrowser's REST API for sessions, scrape and crawl. As with any cloud browser, the browser's own traffic is a WebSocket we never see; this covers what your application asks for and what it is handed back.

name: airtop
label: Airtop
note: Airtop's cloud browser API: sessions, windows and the page content it extracts. The extracted content comes back through this address, so it is inspected before it reaches an agent.

name: notte
label: Notte
note: Notte's browser-agent API for sessions and web actions. Notte echoes a prefix of the token back in its own error messages, so a failed call's body will carry the first characters of whatever was sent.

name: kernel
label: Kernel
note: Kernel's API for hosted browsers and the agents deployed onto them. The company now brands itself kernel.sh; the API address is unchanged.

name: browser-use
label: Browser Use Cloud
note: Browser Use's hosted API for running its browser agent. The self-hosted library talks to a model provider directly and never touches this address, so only the cloud product is covered here.

name: skyvern
label: Skyvern
note: Skyvern's cloud API for browser workflows: starting a run, and polling it for status and output. A self-hosted Skyvern is the customer's own address and needs an upstream of its own.

name: azure-ai-search
template_hint: your search service name, the first label of https://<this>.search.windows.net
label: Azure AI Search
note: One Azure AI Search service: queries and index definitions, with an admin or query key in the api-key header. Microsoft's own guidance is to move to Entra roles instead, and a service with key authentication disabled will refuse this whatever we send. The address holds the customer's own service name, so it is never probed from here.
